title: Sum the first N integers
instructorPromptText: Write a program that asks the user for a positive integer n, then prints the sum of the integers from 1 to n.

specGateDimensions.description: Does the sum include n itself (1+2+...+n) or stop at n-1?
specGateDimensions.rationale: Off-by-one on the upper bound is the classic bug in range-sum problems; the spec must commit to inclusivity before any range() call is written.

specGateDimensions.description: What should the program do if the user enters 0, a negative number, or something that isn't an integer?
specGateDimensions.rationale: The prompt says 'positive integer' but doesn't say what happens when the user disobeys. Forcing a commitment (reprompt, crash, print error, treat as 0) prevents the student from claiming a crash is 'out of scope'.

specGateDimensions.description: What exactly is printed — just the number, or a sentence like 'The sum is X'?
specGateDimensions.rationale: Phase 4 needs something concrete to diff against; 'prints the sum' is ambiguous between bare integer and formatted string.

expectedDivergences.pattern: Student writes `range(1, n)` instead of `range(1, n+1)`, excluding n from the sum
Student forgets to cast input to int, so `input()` returns a string and either concatenation happens or a type error is raised
Plan describes an accumulator loop; code uses `sum(range(1, n+1))` — coherent Pythonic simplification
Plan describes a loop; code uses the closed-form `n*(n+1)//2` — coherent mathematical shortcut
Spec commits to validating positive input but code accepts any integer without checking
